Across and UMA control on PulseChain: a bounded historical audit
Research date: 29 September 2026. This study uses public, read-only contract state, logs, receipts,
historical execution traces and published source. It examines the claim that the examined wallets
acquired control of copied Across and UMA components. It does not attribute addresses to people or
assume that ownership of one component establishes ownership of an entire protocol.
Findings
The subsequent proposal and relay audit (Appendix 46) matches the HubPool ownership proposal to the
execution below by both proposal hash and UMA assertion ID. The undisputed assertion settled after five
days, although its embedded rules excluded HubPool calls. These records establish on-chain execution,
not a valid off-chain Snapshot vote. The later owner-only chain-88888 configuration is also verified there.
T wo control changes are directly established. Across's copied HubPool changed owner to 
0xfeca7291cebe75789ffa707754db259187b1d140 on 19 June 2026. An OptimisticGovernor module attached to
the Across Safe changed owner to the examined e121 wallet, 0x98c89980d1eae247ada3636ae27648f78e66e121,
on 19 August 2026. Successful receipts, actual execution traces and endpoint owner getters agree on
both changes.
The module used UMA's OptimisticOracleV3 while executing each change through the Safe. This is a
specific, observable connection between Across governance, UMA oracle infrastructure and the named
e121 address. It does not mean e121 became owner of the OptimisticOracleV3 contract or of UMA's
Finder, VotingV2 or GovernorV2. Those sampled ownership/role addresses remained unchanged through
the endpoint. T wo GovernorV2 proposals were submitted by e121; proposal submission is distinct from
execution and ownership transfer.
HubPool is an Across component, so “Across and HubPool” should not be counted as two independent
protocol acquisitions. The bounded results support a component-level control map, not a finding that all
Across and UMA authority was transferred to one operator. The supplied 
0xb8698cfffdaaf26ca21fe8aa560c18cc2b2f5996 address was not a direct new owner in the verified changes
below; no shared human ownership is inferred from other research about that address.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 39

Scope and historical boundary
Endpoint: chain 369, block 27,659,393, hash 
0xc5e582cd902f4bff3b1aa325b9b564fcd5d6dc0ffa77a03fcd105b65c6390275. The inherited comparison is block 
17,232,999. Post-fork log searches cover 17,233,000–27,659,393, inclusive. The endpoint block was
re-read and matched. All observations come from https://rpc.pulsechain.com, so these are one-provider
observations rather than independent consensus verification.
Across addresses were discovered from the historical deployment records at commit 
a231a21df4ee58378d3f0fc8148daf5bc4791e3c: HubPool deployment and AcrossConfigStore deployment. The
HubPool deployment names its Finder dependency, which was then checked using the live endpoint
getter. This avoids treating unrelated UMA versions as interchangeable.

The Safe's address is the owner of ConfigStore, but a Safe's capabilities are not described completely by
an owner() field. The recorded traces below demonstrate module-mediated execution. An unchanged
ConfigStore owner address therefore should not be presented as proof that its surrounding governance
path is unchanged. Conversely, ownership of the module is not itself a record that every target
configuration was changed.
The endpoint HubPool owner 0xfeca…d140 has no deployed bytecode at that block. That observation
describes the account at the endpoint; it does not identify who controls it. The endpoint Safe's getOwners()
returns five signer addresses. Those signers are not sufficient on their own to describe the module
execution demonstrated in the receipts.

HubPool ownership changed through an oracle-mediated Safe execution
Transaction 0x6775…04fd succeeded at block 26,822,316, 19 June 2026, 05:46:05 UTC, hash 
0x6c83c1e7ab758bdd30d7fc8c0e245f49ee70c5ffc077528e21bc11e0f69a61de. Its HubPool OwnershipTransferred event
moves ownership from the Across Safe to 0xfeca7291cebe75789ffa707754db259187b1d140; that address is also
the transaction sender and the endpoint owner.
The historical trace shows a call to the module at 0x8692…8991, delegated execution through
implementation 0x28cebfe94a03dbca9d17143e9d2bd1155dc26d5d, interaction with OptimisticOracleV3, a call
through the Safe, and the final HubPool ownership transfer. The receipt records the state-changing
event; the trace supplies the execution path. These are observations of an existing successful
transaction, not a hypothetical administrative capability.
The historical HubPool source assigns its owner multiple administrative functions, including pool routes,
cross-chain contract configuration and other parameters. Identifying that administrative owner is
relevant to interpreting configuration history. It does not imply arbitrary mint authority over each token
the HubPool holds.
The optimistic-governance module changed owner to e121
Transaction 0x703f…bc61 succeeded at block 27,330,450, 19 August 2026, 23:39:05 UTC, hash 
0x0c6a25938fb01f1e3319423a742857f9901a9a16fbf0abacca8bfcb47389258a. Its sender is e121. The module emits 
OwnershipTransferred from the Across Safe to e121, matching the endpoint owner() result.
The historical trace follows the module, OptimisticOracleV3 and the Safe, then returns to the module for
its ownership transfer. Thus the change is more specific than an address merely appearing in a proposal
or event payload. The verified implementation is OptimisticGovernor. Its owner controls settings such as
the proposal rules, liveness, collateral/ bond parameters and escalation-manager configuration. Its
proposal execution logic separately interacts with OptimisticOracleV3 and the avatar/target execution
mechanism.
The searched module history returned 35 logs. This study verifies the material ownership changes and
their execution paths; it does not claim to have audited every proposal's merits or to have established
control of every contract reachable through every module configuration. No occurrence of the supplied 
0xb869…5996 address was found in those returned module logs.
The UMA dependencies are not one interchangeable oracle
HubPool's endpoint finder() is 0x40f941e48a552bf496b154af6bf55725f18d77c3, matching its historical
deployment. Its historical dispute code resolves the SkinnyOptimisticOracle interface. The Safe
governance module instead interacted with OptimisticOracleV3 in the verified transfers. The same
Finder registry names several distinct oracle and support contracts:
Finder interface Address at both comparison blocks
SkinnyOptimisticOracle 0xee3afe347d5c74317041e2618c49534daf887c24
OptimisticOracle 0xc43767f4592df265b4a9f1a398b97ff24f38c6a6
OptimisticOracleV2 0xa0ae6609447e57a42c51b50eae921d701823ffae
OptimisticOracleV3 0xfb55f43fb9f48f63f9269db7dde3bbbe1ebdc0de
Oracle 0x004395edb43efca9885cedad51ec9faf93bd34ac — verified as
VotingV2
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 41

Finder interface Address at both comparison blocks
Store 0x54f44ea3d2e7aa0ac089c4d8f7c93c27844057bf
IdentifierWhitelist 0xcf649d9da4d1362c4daea67573430bd6f945e570
CollateralWhitelist 0xdbf90434df0b98219f87d112f37d74b1d90758c7
Finder ownership is unchanged and its complete post-fork log query returned no events in the bounded
interval. Its verified source separates registry ownership from the individual implementations it returns.
The eight sampled mappings agree at the two comparison blocks. This does not assess every interface
ever registered with UMA or every oracle configuration.
SkinnyOptimisticOracle has a different interface and control structure from an Ownable application
module. It must not be assigned a fictitious owner() because another UMA contract has one.
OptimisticOracleV3 and VotingV2 are separately verified contracts with owner getters; each reports
GovernorV2 at both comparison blocks and returned no ownership-transfer events in the searched
interval.
GovernorV2 proposals and the limits of the ownership claim
The verified GovernorV2 source uses exclusive roles. Its sampled roles are unchanged between the
inherited and endpoint blocks:
Role Holder
Owner, role 0 GovernorV2 itself, 
0x7b292034084a41b9d441b71b6e3557edd0463fa8
Proposer, role 1 0x50efac9619225d7fb4703c5872da978849b6e7cc
Emergency proposer, role 2 0x91f1804acaf87c2d34a34a70be1bb16bb85d6748
The complete GovernorV2 log query returned two NewProposal events in the searched interval, IDs 194
and 195. Their successful submission receipts identify e121 as the transaction sender:
Proposal 194: block 27,331,017, transaction 0x6f0d…d8b0.
Proposal 195: block 27,341,471, transaction 0x2845…c8a8.
No ProposalExecuted or role-reset event was returned from GovernorV2 in this interval. The endpoint role
readings and the emergency-proposer contract's unchanged owner do not establish completed control
transfers corresponding to those submissions. A successful proposal-submission transaction
demonstrates submission, not approval or execution of the proposal's contents.
This audit does not determine voting-token concentration, delegated voting power, the outcome of every
oracle request, or control of every subsidiary contract. Those are distinct potential mechanisms of
influence. It would be incorrect either to call the two submitted proposals proof of whole-UMA ownership,
or to claim unchanged owner getters exclude every other form of governance influence.
Reproduction and interpretation boundary
Raw evidence is preserved in the new ignored batch artifacts/parb-across-control-20260929/. It includes
historical deployment records; inherited/endpoint owner, role and Finder reads; bounded event queries;
the two ownership receipts and their trace_transaction results; submission receipts; and explorer-verified
• 
•

source responses. Files retain the exact RPC request and response. Expected absence of an ABI method
is distinguished from a returned owner value; a receipt's success is distinguished from completion of a
subsequently proposed governance action.
No write transaction, impersonation, message construction, simulated privileged call or configuration
change was performed. The findings establish particular control changes and dependencies. They do not
establish common human ownership, intent, or a minting capability absent from the controlled token's
own contracts.
